summary: One design fix pushed back into Paper on the 'Component --- Text Area' sheet: the focused row's value text carried a raw 14px font size while the two rows above it bound the same value to var(--ui-text-body-md). Rebound to the token. It is the sheet disagreeing with itself rather than a judgement call, which is why it was fixed rather than raised -- 14px and --ui-text-body-md happen to resolve to the same number today, so nothing looked wrong and nothing would have until a brand seed moved the base size and one of the three rows stayed behind. Two further deviations on the same sheet were NOT changed, because each is a decision for design rather than a transcription slip, and both are recorded under needsDesign in textarea.doc.ts where `pnpm design:gaps` collects them: (1) the line-height is a raw 18px on 14px type, a ratio of 1.286 that is off the --ui-leading-* scale entirely (tight 1.25, snug 1.3) -- the component ships leading-snug, the nearest role, 0.2px per line larger, which lands the 6-row box on the sheet's own 128px; the same raw 18px sits on the Input sheet where it is not load-bearing, and here it multiplies down every line of a paragraph; (2) the sheet draws the typed value in --ui-text-secondary while Input ships --ui-text-primary, and Textarea follows Input so that a form holding both does not show two inks for the same thing.

migration.manual: No code change. The Paper sheet now resolves its value type through the token, so a brand seed that moves the base size moves all three rows together.
